definitions.gloss: baseball cap — a soft cap with a stiff visor at the front, worn by baseball players and as casual headwear
definitions.explanation: A cap with a rounded crown and a stiff visor in front, originally designed for baseball players but now widely worn as casual headwear. In Japan the term is used both for the uniform caps of baseball teams and for the everyday fashion item (which is often also called キャップ in modern usage).

examples.japanese: {野球帽|やきゅうぼう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧。
examples.english: To put on a baseball cap.

examples.english: I wore a baseball cap to protect my head from the strong summer sun.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{野球|やきゅう}→野球：04727_yakyuu⟧ ('baseball') and {帽|ぼう} (the on-reading of ⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧, 'hat').

USAGE:
- Refers both to the specific baseball uniform cap and to any visored casual cap of the same shape.
- In modern casual speech, the loanword ⟦キャップ→キャップ：05435_kyappu⟧ is very common and often interchangeable with {野球帽|やきゅうぼう} for everyday wear. {野球帽|やきゅうぼう} emphasizes the baseball-cap shape or origin.
- The verb used for wearing a cap is ⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧, not ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ or きる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {野球帽|やきゅうぼう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧: to put on / wear a baseball cap
- {野球帽|やきゅうぼう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}ぐ→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧: to take off a baseball cap
- ⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{野球帽|やきゅうぼう}: a team baseball cap
- ⟦お{気|き}に{入|い}り→お気に入り：10297_okiniiri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{野球帽|やきゅうぼう}: a favorite baseball cap

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦キャップ→キャップ：05435_kyappu⟧: cap — the more common everyday loanword; often refers to the same kind of visored cap.
- ⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧: hat, cap (general) — covers all headwear, including straw hats, knit caps, and formal hats.
- ハット: hat — usually refers to brimmed fashion hats such as fedoras or bucket hats.
- {麦|むぎ}わら⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧: straw hat — a different style of summer headwear.

REGISTER:
Neutral. ⟦キャップ→キャップ：05435_kyappu⟧ tends to sound more modern and fashion-oriented; {野球帽|やきゅうぼう} is a clearer, more descriptive term often used in writing or when specifying the baseball-style shape.
